thread:
lee: Quick sync — our EU tenant POC surfaced a routing hole for active/active + residency. Some writes are getting routed to us-east during overload. Need a short playbook.
anna: Oof. Is this the case where the edge picks cheapest region without checking tenant residency tag? :grimacing:
raj: Yeah, looks like the smart-router currently considers latency/cost only. We don't have an enforcement gate for resident-only tenants.
marco: TL;DR: we need a policy layer between routing decision and proxy that can veto non-resident targets.
sarah: +1. Proposal: tenant metadata gets a residency enum (EU_ONLY, EU_PREFERRED, GLOBAL) and the router consults it before costing.
lee: Example tenant blob we can standardize:
```
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "residency": "EU_ONLY",
  "require_consent": true
}
```
anna: For EU_ONLY, router must only return EU endpoints. If none available, return explicit error (409 or 451?) with guidance + retry-after header.
raj: I think 451 makes sense for legal restriction. But apps expect a write fallback. We should offer two policies: strict (error) and soft (buffer-and-forward/escrow) controlled by tenant contract.
marco: Soft mode raises complexity: escrowed writes that later get replayed to resident region. Need idempotency keys + ordering guarantees. Can we piggyback on existing tenant write-queue (kinesis-like)?
sarah: We can: create a per-tenant escrow stream in the resident region. When router hits non-resident, it either rejects (strict) or writes to escrow (soft) and returns a synthetic success with header X-Resident-Pending: true.
lee: Important: escrow must be encrypted with tenant KMS in resident region. No plaintext ever leaves residency.
raj: Operationally, we need SLA for escrow replay latency and a compensating flow when replay fails (alert + customer-visible degradation). Also preserve KV cache invariants — don't populate global KV for escrowed writes.
anna: Agreed. Telemetry: metric for "resident_write_rejected", "resident_write_escrowed", and per-tenant last-escrow-age. Add trace tag when router does a residency-eval.
marco: Edge proxy change: inject X-Tenant-Residency header and a flag X-Residence-Mode (strict|soft) so downstream can decide quickly.
sarah: Docs link mockup: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/residency-failover (will create page). Include sample response for strict:
```
HTTP/1.1 451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "tenant_residency_restriction",
  "message": "Writes for this tenant must stay in EU. No EU capacity available.",
  "retry_after": 60
}
```
lee: Action items:
- @anna draft tenant metadata schema + enum (ticket INF-1245)
- @raj design escrow stream + replay semantics (INF-1246)
- @sarah change proxy headers + docs (INF-1247)
- @marco vet KMS restrictions and idempotency pattern (INF-1248)
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary of residency-router v0.3 succeeded in eu-west-1 :rocket:
anna: I'll ping legal about 451 vs 409 just to be safe. :eyes:
marco: One more: fallback policy should be configurable per-route (embeddings vs chat vs batch ingest). Low-risk routes could be soft by default.
sarah: We also need tests: chaos test that kills EU region and asserts strict tenants fail with 451 and soft tenants get X-Resident-Pending header.
lee: Cool. Let's iterate on the RFC. I'll consolidate notes and open a follow-up RFC with a diagram. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
